title: Intelligence graph and guardrails
tagline: Close open privacy and security items first, land the graph work already in flight, get the scheduled jobs green, then hold steady until January.
phase: Step 1 of 4: privacy and security triage
bottomLine: Three weeks of graph, guard, factory and runner work landed fast, faster than it could be reviewed. This track lands it in a fixed order: privacy and security items first, then the scheduled jobs and health checks, then the graph wiring, then a hardening batch. On 11 December it freezes to maintenance until the 5 January review.
healthReason: A production health check has been red since 6 November, the always-on runner is logged out, and privacy items are past their dates.
pathToGreen: On track when every item classed as an exposure is closed and the health check and runner are green, due 25 November.
why: The intelligence graph is the longest-lived asset here: an expanding record of the AI market built from events and public sources. The work outran review, so the next month is about landing it safely rather than widening it.
mission: Classify every open privacy item as an exposure or hardening; close the exposures; get the runner and health checks green with three scheduled jobs; finish the graph wiring already in flight with real consumers; then stop adding scope until January.
destination: On 25 November no exposure-class item is open. On 11 December graph v2 is merged, health checks are green, the runner runs three jobs, and the hardening batch is in. From 12 December to 4 January the track is maintenance only.
showcase: Sequencing by the real constraint: one reviewer's attention, not engineering capacity
Privacy defects treated as defects in every layer, even when a backstop would catch them
A deliberate freeze: new lanes and sources go to one dated January review instead of being dropped or started

decisions.decision: The order inside the track is fixed: exposures, then health checks and the runner, then graph wiring, then hardening.
decisions.why: Privacy items are never dropped, only sequenced, and anything that is a live exposure goes first.

decisions.decision: The agent factory's CI review keeps running. Auto-merge and other factory features wait for January.
decisions.why: It is the one independent review running while human review capacity is the constraint.

decisions.decision: Graph items not on the finish list move to one queue with a single review date, 5 January.
decisions.why: Frozen with an owner and a date, not abandoned.

decisions.decision: The debrief backfill runs here as an unattended job: private records and claims only, no drafts, no CRM.
decisions.why: It is graph work, and it can run without a review session.

open.question: Claim review policy: 2,508 candidates, 43 reviewed.
open.recommendation: Model review on traceability, with Alex sampling 50. Fact-checking stays at the point of use.

open.question: Should research inferences enter the graph as low-confidence leads?
open.recommendation: Admit them flagged as inference, kept out of anything published until checked.

open.question: Does sequencing the rest of the graph to January sit right?
open.recommendation: Yes: review attention is the constraint. If not, the graph takes the second session and the eval study slips.

risks.risk: The track swallows the plan again.
risks.mitigation: One session, a fixed order and a hard stop on 11 December.

risks.risk: A guard change gets waved through.
risks.mitigation: Guard, filter and allowlist diffs are read by a human in one sitting, with self-test output attached.

risks.risk: The runner goes offline over the holidays.
risks.mitigation: Nothing in the plan depends on it between 21 December and 3 January.

assumptions.assumption: The red health check has a fixable cause, not an alarm from a frozen lane.
assumptions.test: Read the failing workflow's last run before changing anything.
